Q: How to correctly extract the CLS token from a Keras Hub ViT backbone, and clarify preprocessor usage and pretraining dataset? A:

Your extraction of the CLS token (features[:, 0, :]) is correct, as the token is added before the sequence of the patches. Since you are using the Backbone class as is, no preprocessor is applied, so you will have to resize and rescale your inputs accordingly. Lastly, the _imagenet preset is trained on ImageNet-1k; to use the larger dataset, just modify your preset string to vit_base_patch16_224_imagenet21k.

Q: WxPython: How do i add a button next to a Node in a Tree A:

Posting for posterity since this is an old question. When you create the panel that holds the "run" buttons, you're setting the parent to be the CustomTreeCtrl's parent. As soon as you trigger a refresh event on the tree item (e.g. clicking it), the button disappears because its panel has been instructed to paint on the tree's parent, which is hidden behind the tree. It being hidden behind the tree also prevents any mouse events from reaching it.

Change panel creation to this (parent => self):

for tc_task in tc_tasks:
    panel = wx.Panel(self, size=(100,25))
    button = wx.Button(parent=panel, size=(100,25), label='run')

etc. Rest of it works fine.

Q: npm ERR! husky - .git can't be found WINDOWS A:

In my case, everything was fine except parent folder of the project had .git.

Husky found a problem as .git in parent folder whereas project in child folder of it.

I removed .git from parent folder as git was mistakenly init in parent folder.

Q: MySQLTransactionRollbackException: Deadlock found when trying to get lock; A:

This is an old question, but maybe somebody finds it useful.

The cause might be that MySQL's InnoDB uses insert intention locks which lock a set of rows when inserting or updating.

Check this link for more information about the different types of locks that InnoDB uses.

This link explains a bit about the deadlocks.

Sometimes it will be almost impossible to prevent these deadlocks. The most common solutions are:

  1. The first option is always operate in the tables in the same order
  2. Reduce the scope (duration) of the transaction to the minimum
  3. If necessary, lock in advance (already done automatically for your case)
  4. Retry the transaction
